paris.title: The most beautiful and famous tourist places in Paris
values: Paris, the French capital, is the most beautiful city in France and the world for tourism. It is the city of light or the city of love, as some like to call it. For decades and until this day, Paris has been one of the leading centers in the world for business, fashion, entertainment, art and culture. Its name is associated with famous international landmarks, museums and cathedrals, and it is the first destination for tourism in France.
Eiffel Tower
/__l5e/assets-v1/7f50cbd8-9711-4b6c-8e80-efafb30a1ef7/eiffel-tower.webp

The Eiffel Tower in Paris is one of the prominent tourist landmarks in Paris, if not all of France. It was built in 1889 by the engineer Gustave Eiffel. The Eiffel Tower is 324 meters high and is the tallest building in the capital, Paris, absolutely. In addition, it is one of the most visited tourist places in Paris. Read more
Champs-Élysées Street
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/6d/Avenue_des_Champs-%C3%89lys%C3%A9es_July_24%2C_2009_N1.jpg

The Champs-Élysées Street in Paris is one of the most famous and longest French streets, and it is one of the most prestigious and luxurious tourist and commercial streets in the world. The street contains the finest international commercial stores and upscale restaurants, and there are many cafes on the sidewalks and side streets. It is classified as one of the most important tourist places in Paris. Read more
Arc de Triomphe
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/79/Arc_de_Triomphe%2C_Paris_21_October_2010.jpg

The Arc de Triomphe in Paris is an arch located at the beginning of the famous Champs-Élysées street in Charles de Gaulle Square, or what was known as the Place de l'Étoile in the heart of the capital Paris. The Arc de Triomphe is considered one of Paris's famous tourist landmarks and one of the city's most important symbols after the famous Eiffel Tower, which enjoys special popularity. The arch's height is 50 meters... Read More
Place de la Concorde
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fa/Place_de_la_Concorde_from_the_Eiffel_Tower%2C_Paris_April_2011.jpg

Place de la Concorde is one of the largest squares and plazas in the French capital, Paris. The Place de la Concorde is located at the eastern end of the Champs-Elysées. The square contains a huge Egyptian obelisk gifted by Khedive Ismail to Louis Philippe in 1831. It is considered one of the most prominent tourist places in Paris.
The Latin Quarter
/__l5e/assets-v1/404a7b7d-f606-41da-8e1a-52befacb1ec2/place-du-terre-paris.jpg

The Latin Quarter is considered one of the most famous and also one of the oldest tourist spots in Paris. It is located on the left bank of the Seine River, where it includes a large number of historical buildings. It also offers its tourist visitors the pleasure of exploring authentic Parisian life through French restaurants, cafes, and the most famous French and international fashion brands... Read more
Paris Disneyland
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/8/88/Sleeping_Beauty_Castle%2C_Disneyland%2C_Paris.jpg

Paris Disneyland, also called Disneyland Resort Paris or Euro Disney, is considered one of Paris's entertainment landmarks. It is located 32 km from the center of the French capital, Paris. Disneyland includes two amusement parks and 7 hotels, all owned by the Walt Disney Company. It is considered the second largest Disneyland city outside the United States of America after Tokyo Disneyland... Read More
The Louvre Museum
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/66/Louvre_Museum_Wikimedia_Commons.jpg

The Louvre Museum is one of the largest museums in the world and the most famous museum in Paris. It is an important landmark in the heart of Paris, France. Around 35,000 objects from prehistoric times to the 21st century are displayed over an area of 60,600 square meters. Read more
Picasso Museum
/__l5e/assets-v1/960d8683-0c13-4c60-8a0d-2d699e0e6903/musee-picasso-paris.jpg

The Picasso Museum in Paris is the second-largest museum dedicated to the international artist Picasso, after the Picasso Museum in Barcelona, Spain. The building of the Picasso Museum in Paris was built in 1659, meaning the museum building dates back to the 17th century AD and was originally a palace. It changed into a school and its ownership transferred to many individuals before the French Revolutionary government took control of it. It is considered one of the most famous museums in Paris. Read more
Luxembourg Gardens
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/92/LuxembourgMontparnasse.JPG

Jardin du Luxembourg, or Luxembourg Gardens, is the second largest public garden in Paris. The garden covers an area of 224,500 square meters. The garden is famous for its peaceful atmosphere with surrounding ponds in terraces with balustrades that feature a series of statues of former French queens and saints and ancient copies.
Jardin des Plantes
/__l5e/assets-v1/6ac13bbd-52f1-4c07-a260-3341aae77e82/jardin-des-plantes-paris.jpg

The Jardin des Plantes in Paris is one of the most important gardens in Paris and is located not far from two important landmarks for Arab tourists: the Islamic Institute (which houses the largest mosques in Paris), and the Institute of the Arab World.
Versailles Palace
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/95/Vue_a%C3%A9rienne_du_domaine_de_Versailles_par_ToucanWings_-_Creative_Commons_By_Sa_3.0_-_081_%28cropped%29.jpg

Versailles Palace in Paris is considered one of the most beautiful palaces in Paris and France in general. This palace was built in 1624 and is located 20 kilometers south of Paris. Versailles Palace is distinguished by the presence of the famous Hall of Mirrors, and it also contains thousands of amazing paintings and artworks. The palace is an example of architectural art in France... Read more
Open daily from 09:00 AM to 06:30 PM, ticket price is 80 Euros, which is equivalent to 96.85 US dollars.
Palais Garnier
/__l5e/assets-v1/2edcf21d-1f2d-4503-b913-bee174d4be06/palais-garnier-paris.avif

The Palais Garnier, also known as the Paris Opera House, is located in a magnificent and extremely splendid building that was established by Louis XIV in 1669 at the request of Napoleon III as part of the campaign to rebuild Paris. The Paris Opera House is the largest among opera houses in the world... Read more
Élysée Palace
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/58/Secretary_Pompeo_Arrives_to_Meet_with_French_Foreign_Minister_Le_Drian_in_Paris_%2850610423656%29_%28cropped%29.jpg

The Élysée Palace is one of the most famous palaces in Paris and is the official residence of the President of the French Republic. It houses the office of the head of state and the meeting place for the Council of Ministers. The Élysée Palace is located near the famous Champs-Élysées in Paris. The palace was built in the eighteenth century and has undergone many modifications over the following centuries, but it has preserved its classic design... Read more

values: Learn all about the tourist city of Marseille
On this page, you will learn the following:
Marseille city in general
The best time and ideal duration to travel to Marseille
Tourism in the city of Marseille
History, climate, geography, and sports of Marseille city
Marseille in general

Marseille is one of the most important French cities. It has gained this importance due to several factors, including being the second-largest urban area in France, after Paris, of course. It also holds a prominent position in France's tourism lists, as it is considered the largest French coastal city, located on France's southern coast. It boasts the Port of Marseille, which is considered the largest seaport in France, in addition to its cultural significance and the city's role in it, as it was chosen in 2013 as the European Capital of Culture. Above all, it has almost the largest Arab Muslim community in France.

This city is considered one of the main centers in the industrial and commercial fields, thanks to the Port of Marseille and Marseille Airport, which is considered the fourth largest airport in France. Marseille has taken a large share of tourism in France, as it is a city famous for its beaches, seas, architecture, buildings, exhibitions, markets, and museums, where there are more than 24 museums and 42 theaters. It is one of the suitable cities for travel, whether you are alone or with your loved ones.
The best time to travel to Marseille

The best time for travel and tourism in Marseille, France, is during spring and summer, meaning from March to August. This is when the temperatures are moderate and warm, allowing you to stroll freely. You can practice many enjoyable activities in these ideal tourist conditions, such as water sports, boating, and attending French festivals filled with live music.
The ideal duration for tourism in Marseille

The ideal duration for travel and tourism in Marseille, France, is approximately three days. During these days, you can visit the neighboring villages, explore the city's natural wonders, and spend a lot of time by the sea to relax. You will also be able to visit Marseille's most prominent landmarks, such as the Old Port, the Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations (MuCEM), climb slopes, and stroll amidst the beautiful lavender fields, among many other recreational and tourist activities.
Notre Dame de la Garde Basilica
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a1/Notre-Dame_de_la_Garde_aerial_view_2020.jpeg

Due to its grandeur, the famous writer Victor Hugo chose it as the setting for his novel The Hunchback of Notre Dame, to unleash his humanity from behind the walls of this cathedral where he found warmth and love.

It is Notre Dame de Paris Cathedral, meaning the Cathedral of Our Lady, and it is a Catholic cathedral dating back to the Middle Ages, located on the Seine River, and it is one of the most magnificent examples of French Gothic architecture. It is also one of the most famous Catholic Church buildings in France and in the world.

Inside, it contains some of the most important Catholic relics, such as the supposed Crown of Thorns, a splinter from the True Cross, and one of the Holy Nails, which is why this cathedral receives a very high number of visitors.
The Old Port
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/74/Marseille_Old_Port.jpg
This port is located at the end of Canebière street, which is considered the main street and popular place in Marseille, and it includes around it a number of important and prominent landmarks.

Among these landmarks are Saint Victor's Abbey, which is considered one of the oldest Christian places of worship in France, The Hotel de Ville (City Hall), the historic ferry that sails between the opposite sides of the Old Port, and the famous Roman Dock Museum. So, when you travel to France, you must visit this beautiful port and see its historical landmarks.
Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/fr/0/01/Mucem%2C_Marseille.jpeg

Every country has a museum that embodies its past, and every city has a museum that commemorates its past. But to find a museum that commemorates and preserves different civilizations, that is truly a marvel.

The Museum of European Civilizations, located in the city of Marseille, is considered one of the great symbols of the city of Marseille, and a focal point for those intending to visit France. It was inaugurated in 2013, the same year Marseille was classified as the European Capital of Culture.

This museum is dedicated to European and Mediterranean civilizations, through the historical and cultural exchange in the Mediterranean basin. The museum, which was built from stone, water, and wind, is designed in the shape of a cube with a size of 15,000 square meters, and includes exhibitions, underground celebration halls, a book library, and a restaurant.
Noailles Market

Noailles Market is a wonderful and lively place in the French city of Marseille. If you are a fan of shopping tours, you can shop there and buy multi-colored fabrics, various types of African and Indian food and spices, household items, accessories, and many other things.
/__l5e/assets-v1/f1c88381-eb5d-4795-8e12-42fb0b84e029/marche-de-noailles-marseille.jpg
Le Panier District
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c8/Rue_Panier_Marseille.jpg

Le Panier is the oldest district in the city of Marseille, and it is considered the historical center and cultural heart of the city. This colorful district is also located in a wonderful location on a hill above the Old Port.

It is one of the most beautiful tourist places in Marseille, France. You can enjoy strolling through its old, stone-paved, sloping, and narrow streets in the old city, as well as taking photos of the murals on the sides of the beautifully colored buildings, and discovering local artisan shops, food stores, and art galleries.
Calanques National Park
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7a/En-Vau_calanque_4.jpg
Calanques National Park is a wonderful natural site where the Mediterranean Sea meets the rocky Calanques mountains.

It is one of the important tourist attractions in the city of Marseille that we recommend you visit. The park offers you the opportunity to enjoy natural landscapes, majestic limestone rock walls, with coves full of enchanting turquoise saltwater pools, in addition to practicing many outdoor sports activities such as swimming, kayaking, boating, yachting on a romantic trip, long-distance walking, and rock climbing.
Marseille

Marseille is the second-largest city in France after the capital Paris, with a population of over 850,000 within its administrative boundaries alone, which cover an area of 240.62 square kilometers. Marseille is located on the southern coast of France overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, and the population of the greater Marseille area exceeds 1.7 million. Marseille's port is France's largest commercial port. Marseille is the capital of both the Bouches-du-Rhône department and the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region. Marseille was chosen as the European Capital of Culture for 2013. The city is famous for having a large Arab and Islamic community, and researchers believe that Marseille could become the first Muslim-majority city in Western Europe.
Geography of Marseille

Marseille is the second largest city in France after Paris, the capital, and it is also the center of the second largest urban area after Paris. To its south is the Mediterranean Sea, and to its north is the Sainte-Victoire mountain range. To its east are rugged coastal areas interspersed with a small fjord, as well as the Sainte-Baume mountain range, a forest of deciduous trees, and the city of Toulon, in addition to the French Riviera. To its west is the Gulf of Lion and the Camargue region located in the Rhône Delta. Marseille Airport is located northwest of the city. In the Bay of Marseille is the Frioul Archipelago, which consists of four islands, one of which is the site of Château d'If, which became famous due to Alexandre Dumas' novel The Count of Monte Cristo.
Marseille Climate

Marseille's climate is Mediterranean, with mild and humid winters, while summers are warm to hot and mostly dry. December, January, and February are the coldest months of the year, with an average temperature of 12 degrees Celsius during the day and 4 degrees Celsius at night. July and August are the hottest months of the year, with an average temperature of about 30 degrees Celsius during the day and 19 degrees Celsius at night at Marseille Airport (which is 35 km from the city), while the average temperature in the city is about 27 degrees Celsius in July. The city is exposed to the Mistral winds (especially in winter and spring), which are strong, cold winds coming from the Rhône Valley and are usually dry. The city is also exposed to hot, dust-laden Sirocco winds coming from the Sahara Desert.
Rainfall in Marseille averages 515 mm annually, with September being the wettest month, receiving 77.1 mm of rain. July is the driest month, with only 9.2 mm of rain.
History of Marseille

Humans have inhabited the city of Marseille and its surrounding areas for approximately 30,000 years. Cave paintings discovered in Marseille in the late 20th century date back to between 27,000 and 19,000 BC. Recent excavations have also uncovered brick dwellings dating to approximately 6000 BC near the railway station.

Marseille is known as France's oldest city. It was founded by the Greeks (who came from an area now known as Phocaea in far western Turkey) around 600 BC as a trading port and named Massalia. The relationship between this Greek city and Massalia is mentioned in the first book of Thucydides' History of the Peloponnesian War.

Massalia was one of the first Greek ports in Western Europe, with a population of over a thousand. Massalia was the first settlement to develop into a city in France. The new city faced danger due to an alliance of Etruscans, Carthaginians, and Celts against it. The city fortified itself, especially with the rise of the Roman Republic at that time. By 500 BC, the city flourished as a link between Gaul and steadily exported goods and wine. Rome felt it needed slaves and new products, so Julius Caesar occupied Massalia after it sided with his enemy, Pompey the Great. The city lost its independence for the first time in 49 BC. One Roman man, Titus Annius Milo, was exiled to Marseille and jokingly said that he did not regret leaving Rome as long as he could eat red mullet in Marseille.
After the city fell into the hands of Roman forces following a naval battle, the fleet was confiscated by Roman authorities, and the city was named Massilia during the Roman era.

Most of the archaeological remains from the Greek period were replaced by later Roman additions. Marseille adapted well to its new situation under Roman rule. During the Roman era, the city was governed by 15 elected members from a total of 600 senators, three of whom held executive power. Among the laws enacted by the council were prohibiting women from drinking wine and allowing assistance to people for suicide.

Christianity later appeared in Marseille, evidenced by catacombs and Roman martyrologies. According to Provence traditions, Mary Magdalene, accompanied by her brother Lazarus, evangelized in Marseille. The Diocese of Marseille was established in the 1st century AD.
Tourism in Marseille

Marseille's port is one of the most important means of transport to the city, with 2.4 million passengers passing through it annually. Marseille has many features that have made it one of France's major tourist cities, as the city is characterized by its beaches, history, architecture, and culture (it has 24 museums and 42 theaters). The number of visitors to the city reached 4.1 million in 2012. Marseille ranked 86th among the world's most attractive cities for business tourism, after being in 150th place the previous year. Many urban projects are being developed, including parks, museums, public places, and real estate projects to make the city more attractive. The municipality of Marseille works to be a major entertainment center in the south of the country, with a high focus on museums, cinemas, theaters, clubs, pubs, restaurants, fashion shops, hotels, and art exhibitions.
Sports in Marseille

Marseille hosts a variety of teams and sports facilities. The most popular sports team in the city is the Olympique Marseille football club, which won the European Champions League in 1992-1993 and was runner-up in 1991. It also reached the final of the UEFA Cup in 1999 and 2004.

The club's stadium is Stade Vélodrome, which can accommodate more than 60,000 spectators and hosts many different sports events, such as matches of the French national rugby team. The stadium hosted several matches during the 1998 FIFA World Cup and the 2007 Rugby World Cup. The city is also famous for its pétanque activities, so much so that it is known as the capital of pétanque. The city hosted the World Pétanque Championship in 2012, and the Marseille Pétanque Mondial is held there annually, which is the most important tournament in this sport.

Sailing races are one of the important sports in Marseille, as the wind conditions allow these competitions to be held in the warm waters of the Mediterranean Sea. Many other water sports are held in Marseille, such as surfing. Marseille has three golf courses, as well as dozens of sports halls and many public swimming pools. Running is also popular among the city's residents in public parks.

History of Lyon
Lyon in general

The city of Lyon is considered the capital of the Rhône-Alpes region, located in southeastern France. It holds great importance as the second-largest urban area in France and is famous for its historical and cultural landmarks. It has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, in addition to playing a prominent role in the field of cinema. It is also known for the Festival of Lights and global culinary arts.

Lyon occupies an important strategic location, as it is located at the confluence of the Rhône and Saône rivers. This city is characterized by its climate, which combines oceanic and semi-circular climates, and it is considered one of France's cold regions in winter, but that has not prevented tourists in France from visiting this wonderful city, and seeing its archaeological and civilizational landmarks, and learning about its culture, history, and present, by visiting museums, restaurants, and hotels, and attending the festivals and events that are held annually there.
Parc de la Tête d'Or
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/56/Parc_de_la_T%C3%AAte_d%27Or_Vue_sur_le_lac7.jpg

It is a very large urban park, with an area of 117 hectares. Due to the scarcity of other parks in Lyon, this park has gained great popularity and widespread fame, especially with the presence of the beautiful lake, and the views of the moving boats in it.

For sports lovers, such as walking and running, or cyclists, it is the best place for them. Due to the large turnout of people to visit this park, a large zoo has been placed in it, containing giraffes, elephants, deer, reptiles, and others. So pack your bags when you intend to travel in France, and get ready to enjoy this wonderful park.
Museum of Popular Traditions
/__l5e/assets-v1/5a6b6b94-1180-4116-8708-569a9ae49f21/lyon-musee-gadagne.jpg

We often hear about museums, such as the Chocolate Museum, and it is very strange to find a museum for chocolate, but even stranger is a museum for popular traditions. I wonder if traditions are embodied and placed in museums as a subject? No, but this museum should be placed in another museum because it is a masterpiece in itself. This museum is located in the center of Lyon, and most of its collections focus on the popular events and activities of people from the present and the past.
Place Bellecour
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/99/Place_Bellecour_%28Lyon%2C_2024%2C_version_recentr%C3%A9e_2%29.jpg

It is a large square located in the center of Lyon, and is considered one of the largest open squares in France, and the largest pedestrian square in it. In the middle of the garden stands an equestrian statue of King Louis XIV.

It also contains two wings: the first wing includes the Lyon Tourist Information Office, and the second wing includes an art exhibition. The square has also been included in the UNESCO World Heritage List.
Old City
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4b/Vieuxlyon_saintjean_toits.jpg

The old city of Lyon is an ideal place to enjoy the history of the city of Lyon, with amazing buildings and churches that date back thousands of years, as Lyon's past illuminates this side of the city.

Join a free walking tour in Old Lyon, which boasts narrow cobblestone streets with charming shops, grocery stores, restaurants, and charming cafes. You can walk through the secret passages, called traboules, that connect the different streets. These were used by silk workers during the Renaissance to protect their goods from stormy weather when Lyon was a center of silk industry.

When visiting the old city, you can enter Saint-Jean Cathedral, which is an excellent example of Gothic architecture, and discover the splendor of the charming engineering architecture in the city, which contributed to the inclusion of Lyon as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
History of Lyon

Lyon, which Arabs called Ludoun and Lutoun, is the third largest city in terms of population after Paris and Marseille, and is the capital of the Rhône region and the Rhône-Alpes region in the southeast of the country.

Located between the cities of Paris and Marseille, Lyon is 470 km from Paris, 320 km from Marseille, 160 km from Geneva, 280 km from Turin, and 600 km from Barcelona. It is where the Rhône and Saône rivers meet.

Lyon is divided into nine arrondissements and is famous for its textile industry, especially silk and rayon. The city has a large number of spinning, weaving, and dyeing companies. It is also famous for its automotive, chemical, and electrical industries, as well as agricultural products. In 1998, UNESCO classified the old city of Lyon as a World Heritage Site. It is also home to the headquarters of Interpol.

The city of Lyon was built near the mouth of the Rhône River and became the capital of ancient Gaul. It is currently considered the oldest Roman archaeological site after Rome itself. It is located at the deepest point of the Rhône Valley and is considered the capital of silk, where the Jacquard weaving method was invented. It is currently the capital of the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region, and it enjoys a unique location in the center of Europe. It is a large city bustling with factories, commercial establishments, and markets. The city of Lyon owes its unique character to its surrounding areas, such as the towering hills, vast plains, and the two rivers that surround it. The city includes many cultural institutions that contribute to enhancing its international reputation, including the Opéra de Lyon, the Institut Lumière, and 27 museums. The city also houses the Musée des Beaux-Arts, which occupies the site of the former Abbey of the Benedictines (Saint-Pierre Palace) and is a miniature version of the Louvre Museum.

The city also has 30 of the finest restaurants. There are also covered passages that connect one street to another through squares and buildings. It can be reached from Arab countries via Lyon International Airport or Geneva Airport, which is 4 to 5 hours away. The city is connected by an extensive railway network that links it to its neighboring cities. It was named the “City of Two Rivers” because it is the confluence of the Rhône and Saône rivers. After Paris and Marseille, it is the third-largest French city by population, with 483,181 inhabitants, while in its surrounding urban areas, the population is 1,422,331. It is considered the administrative capital of the Rhône and the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region.

Cannes in general

Next to the aforementioned city of Nice, in the south, lies the French city of Cannes, which has earned the title of the city of the rich, and rightly so, as it is the most visited place by most of the world's celebrities. Its name has been associated with the wealthy class, including millionaires, businessmen, artists, and world-renowned figures, given the city hosts international festivals and conferences, and what it also contains of high-end hotels and restaurants, and famous museums, the most famous of which is the Castre Museum, and its unique collections.

For world celebrities, their representatives, and artists to gather in one place, that is an almost impossible matter, but no, it is not impossible, here in France anything is possible.

La Malmaison Museum, with its sea view in the French city of Cannes and the historical and cultural value it holds within its walls, makes La Malmaison Museum, France, one of the most beautiful and magnificent museums in France ever.

It guarantees you an enjoyable, entertaining, and cultural tour, in addition to a large number of things that you will greatly enjoy when you see them. La Malmaison Museum in Cannes is located one kilometer from the city and is dedicated to displaying a large number of treasures found in the sea. Some of these treasures and artifacts date back to the Roman Empire era, so the museum can be called a historical place in addition to its cultural and civilizational importance.
The Old City
/__l5e/assets-v1/c3dc3947-9370-4979-bfc5-e7893aa83705/cannes-old-town.jpg

Far from the hustle and bustle, and the manifestations of luxurious life, many of those who intend to travel to France and tourism in France intend to stay away from noisy places, and in the city of Cannes in France is their destination, especially in the old city, which was an ancient fishing village, and whose buildings date back to nearly 100 years ago.
The largest part of this city is for pedestrians, who love to wander in small shops, and pass by restaurants with delicious smells, old stairs and a romantic atmosphere.
Villa Domergue
/__l5e/assets-v1/1598e5b1-092b-4af9-8457-832e1f5e5248/cannes-villa-domergue.jpg
Villa Domergue is a testament to the history of modern Art Deco art. The place was designed and implemented by the painter Jean-Gabriel Domergue in 1926.

The villa was listed as a historical site in 1990 due to the splendor and elegance of its design and the outdoor area of the villa. In the villa's garden, there are many ancient busts and some wonderful artworks by the painter's wife, Odette Maugendre-Villers.

Some social and official events of the city, such as art exhibitions, are held at the venue. Enjoy a tour inside the villa and see the splendor and elegance of its design, as well as the busts in the garden. The villa was a meeting place for the official arbitration committee of the Cannes Film Festival, and now it has become a space for art and cultural seminars.
History of Cannes

Cannes is a French city overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, located in the south near the city of Nice. Its population is approximately 70,000. Cannes is known as a tourist center for the upper classes, in addition to annually hosting the Cannes Film Festival during May of each year.

And television program markets such as MIPTV MEDIA in April of each year, and Mipcom in October of each year, and many other exhibitions and festivals. Cannes is considered the second artistic facade in France after Paris.

Colmar city in general
Tourism in Colmar city
History of Colmar city
Colmar in general
Colmar is a city and commune in the Haut-Rhin department and the Grand Est region in northeastern France in the cultural region of Alsace. Its population is approximately 150,000 people.

It is considered the capital of the Upper Rhine region, and this city is famous for its rural villages, ancient towns, cultural landmarks, and museums. This city overlooks the Launch River and is connected to the Rhine River through a canal. Colmar enjoys a sunny climate, but it is considered one of the driest cities in France due to its proximity to the nearby mountain ranges. Some people refer to this city as "Little Venice" due to its similarity to Venice. It also enjoys a high degree of overall tourism in France, as it is a homogeneous city known among tourists for its diverse religious, architectural, and cultural landmarks.
Old Colmar City
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/85/View_of_%C3%89glise_Saint-Martin_%2843833049001%29.jpg

The rural atmosphere of the city can be found here in the old city of Colmar, which has managed to preserve its wonderful and simple rural charm. It also offers those who travel to France a magical glimpse into 1000 years of European history through its cultural heritage.
And when you walk in its streets, you will find old half-timbered houses, beautiful canals, the thriving pedestrian city center, restaurants and shops.
Miniature Venice
/__l5e/assets-v1/033dedb3-ed02-4929-b7c4-48a0af72ea6b/colmar-quai-de-la-poissonnerie.jpg

In Colmar, everything is reasonable. We brought Italian Venice and placed it in Colmar, and it was named Little Venice. This area is considered one of Colmar's symbols, which combines French and German cultures, and from which the Italian flavor emanates, a special flavor of Italian Venice through the tremendous waterways and bridges that cross over the Launch River, and the small boats that sail between its canals.
Unterlinden Museum
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/dd/Musee_d_Unterlinden_colmar.jpg

This museum is located in the Dominican Sisters' Convent, and it features a large and wonderful collection of local and international artistic works and handicrafts from prehistoric times to contemporary eras. The museum holds the French quality mark and is considered one of the most visited museums in France.
In 2009, work began on developing and expanding the museum, and the new building was opened in 2016 in the presence of French President François Hollande.
Maison des Têtes

Also known as the Council of the Presidents, its construction dates back to the 16th century. It is considered one of the oldest wooden buildings in the city of Colmar, and it is characterized by the presence of pictures and faces of the city's most prominent figures, and it contains wonderful wall paintings.
Dominican Church
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9b/Cloitre_colmar.jpg

The church is considered one of the most beautiful buildings in Colmar, as it was built in the old architectural style dating back to the Renaissance era. What distinguishes it is its construction with wonderful pink stones, and its containing the famous Schongauer painting, which made it one of the best tourist attractions in French Colmar.
History of Colmar

Colmar was founded in the 9th century, and in 1354, it joined the city of Décapole. The city adopted the Protestant Reformation in 1575. After a long period and during the Thirty Years' War, the congress was transferred by the Swedish army in 1632, and it was held for two years.

France took control of the city during the reign of King Louis XIV in 1673 CE, and formally ceded it in 1679 CE, before the Treaties of Nijmegen, along with the rest of Alsace. Colmar was then incorporated into the newly formed German Empire in 1871 CE as a result of the Franco-Prussian War and merged into the province of Alsace-Lorraine.

Colmar returned to France after World War I, according to the Treaty of Versailles in 1919 CE. It was then annexed by Nazi Germany in 1940 CE, before returning to French control after the Colmar Pocket battle in 1945 CE. Colmar has been under conservative party rule since 1947 CE.
Geography of Colmar

Colmar extends 64 kilometers to the south and southwest of Strasbourg, where it overlooks a tributary of the Lauch River, which lies directly to the east of the Vosges Mountains and is connected to the Rhine River on the eastern side of the canal.

annecy.title: Learn all about the tourist city of Annecy
values: Learn about everything related to the tourist city of Annecy
On this page, you will learn the following:
The city of Annecy in general
Tourism in the city of Annecy
History of the city of Annecy
Annecy in general

This city is considered one of the largest cities located in southeastern France on the northern edge of Lake Annecy. Many call it the "Pearl of the French Alps", as it is located in the middle between the lakes and the mountains. Others also call it "Venice of the Alps", due to its unique location, which it acquired from the rivers, lakes, and canals surrounding it.

Annecy is 55 km from Paris, while it is 43 km from Geneva, the capital of Switzerland. In Annecy, you are in between, between heaven and heaven, the heaven of France and the heaven of Switzerland. However, you are actually in a third heaven. This city contains prominent landmarks that attract tourists in France, such as: Mount Semnoz, Lake Annecy, Palais de l'Isle, Annecy Castle, Pont des Amours, Imperial Palace, and others.
Lake Annecy
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/20/Boat_%40_Compagnie_des_Bateaux_du_Lac_d%27Annecy_%40_Lake_Annecy_%40_Saint-Jorioz_%2850488289926%29.jpg

It is the third largest lake in France, and it is a famous tourist destination nicknamed the cleanest lake in Europe, due to the cleanliness of the lake and its depth, which reaches 82 meters, and its length, which is 14 km, and its width of 4 km.

This lake is also characterized by its cold waters in summer, which made it a tourist destination in France in the summer. The lake is surrounded by beautiful towns and villages, including: the village of Menthon-Saint-Bernard, Sévrier, Talloires, and others.
https://maps.app.goo.gl/sw7p6awwobLPveuNA?g_st=ic
Pont des Arts (Love Lock Bridge)
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/da/0306_Annecy_-_Pont_des_Amours.jpg

We promised each other that one of us would love the other for the rest of their lives, and that only death would separate us. This promise was not written down, but rather it must be documented on the Love Lock Bridge, or the Lovers' Bridge, by placing a closed lock on this bridge to indicate the impossibility of separation.

This bridge is located in the city of Annecy, and it crosses the Vassé Canal in central France. Due to the large number of locks on the bridge, it was decided to remove the locks to protect the bridge from collapsing, and it was maintained. It has been included in the French National Heritage list.

The Pont des Amours (Love Bridge) over the Vassé Canal connects the Jardins de l'Europe (Gardens of Europe) in Pâquier, and it is a wonderful example of typical architectural engineering from the early twentieth century.
Palais de l'Isle
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/39/Palais_de_l%27Isle_-_Annecy_6-9-2017_10-19-19.JPG
It is an old fortified house that was used as a prison. It has undergone several renovation and restoration operations. It contains old fortified halls and ancient prisoners' cells.

In addition to the old church, semicircular domed rooms, and a large public hall, there is also a spiral staircase connecting the floors. This palace has been classified as a World Heritage site, and the palace is accessed and entered via a drawbridge.
Gardens of Europe
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/57/Jardin_de_l%27Europe_-_Annecy.JPG

One of the most important tourist attractions in Annecy, characterized by its large area, its location on the banks of Lake Annecy, and its natural beauty, where you will find many types of trees and wonderful plants.

The Jardins de l'Europe (Gardens of Europe) is an ideal place for families, as it has seating areas, picnic spots, and a dedicated children's area with many entertaining recreational games. The garden also features many amazing stone statues and beautiful fountains, in addition to a sundial dating back to the nineteenth century, located on Napoleon III's embankment.
Mount Semnoz
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/73/Semnoz_%40_Lac_d%27Annecy_%40_Annecy-le-Vieux_%2834804245794%29.jpg

Mount Semnoz is located in the city of Annecy within the Bauges massif in the Alps. The peaks' elevations vary between 1530 meters at Grand Dan peak and reaching 1699 meters at Crêt de Châtillon peak.
The mountain offers stunning views of the city, the surrounding lakes, and the beautiful green meadows, making it a favorite hiking destination for both locals and city visitors.

Mount Semnoz offers the opportunity to engage in many activities, where you can practice hiking amidst nature and breathe in the fresh air, or go cycling. Horse lovers can also enjoy a wonderful horseback ride and enjoy the enchanting natural scenery.

And if you are an adventure and experience lover, you will find what you are looking for at the summit of Mount Semnoz, where you can experience skydiving or ride the chairlifts and go on a wonderful trip above the mountain. Also, on the mountain, there is a deer park and many recreational games suitable for all ages.
History of Annecy

Annecy is the prefecture and largest city in the Haute-Savoie department in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region in southeastern France. It is located on the northern tip of Lake Annecy, 35 kilometers south of Geneva, nicknamed the "Pearl of the French Alps" in Raoul Blanchard's study, which describes its location between the lake and the mountains. The city controls the northern entrance to the lake narrows. Due to the lack of available building land between the lake and the protected Mount Semnoz, its population remained stagnant, around 50,000 inhabitants, since 1950. However, the 2017 merger with several former communes led to an increase in the city's population to 124,401 inhabitants and its urban area to 203,078 inhabitants, placing Annecy in the sixth position in the region behind Annemasse, which had a population of 292,000 inhabitants.

The Old Town is the heart of commercial and political life in Annecy, traversed by numerous canals and pedestrian streets, including Rue Sainte-Claire, considered one of the most beautiful with its romantic arches from the 17th and 18th centuries. Old Annecy is dotted with many fountains, including the Saint-Jean well, which was moved to the intersection of Rue Carnot and Rue Royale.

Moving from the Count of Genevois in the 13th century to the Count of Savoy in the 14th century, the city became the capital of Savoy in 1434 during the Geneva-Nemours concession until 1659. Its role increased in 1536 during the Calvinist Reformation in Geneva, while the bishop sought refuge in Annecy. Saint Francis de Sales in Annecy gave it its advanced role in the Catholic castle known as the Counter-Reformation. The annexation of Savoy led to the city's incorporation into France in 1860.

This poetic and tourist representation, sometimes called the "Venice of the Alps," comes from the three canals and the Thiou River, which flows through the old city and whose primary role was to protect the city and enable handicrafts. The city witnessed industrial development in the 19th century with the silk industry.

Since the end of the 19th century, Annecy has developed tourism around its summer lake facilities, the proximity of winter resorts, and cultural attraction with the renovation of the castle and the Fine Arts Museum, which opened in 1956, and the Animated Film Festival since 1960, hosted by the Cultural Center in Bonlieu. The municipal environmental policy has succeeded in preserving 40.3% of green spaces, and the city received the Golden Flower in 2015, awarded to France's nine most prosperous cities. Its educational sector has grown since the establishment of the University of Savoy in 1973.

strasbourg.title: Learn all about the tourist city of Strasbourg

On this page, you will learn the following:
Components of Strasbourg city
Tourism in Strasbourg city
History of Strasbourg city
Strasbourg in general
Components of Strasbourg city

The city of Strasbourg is located in eastern France, near the German border, on the Ill River, which is a tributary of the Rhine River. It enjoys an oceanic climate characterized by high temperatures in summer and cold winters. The city of Strasbourg also holds global political importance, as it is the seat of the Parliament and many European institutions.

Culturally, the city of Strasbourg also plays a prominent role, as it has been designated a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. It houses the second-largest university in France, the University of Strasbourg, and is also home to the largest Islamic place of worship in France, the Grand Mosque of Strasbourg.

Economically, Strasbourg is an important center for manufacturing and engineering, and a hub for road and rail transport. The Port of Strasbourg is the second-largest port on the Rhine River. Therefore, the city of Strasbourg deserves a visit from anyone intending to tour France, to fill their soul with the meanings of human civilization.
Strasbourg Cathedral
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7e/Strasbourg_Cathedral_Exterior_-_Diliff.jpg

The writer Victor Hugo described it as a "gigantic and delicate marvel," while Goethe called it a "tall and slender spire, like a vast tree from God." All this was said about Strasbourg Cathedral, or as it is also called, the Cathedral of Our Lady, the Roman Catholic, whose antiquity dates back to the 13th century AD.

Among the wonders and beauty of its construction is that it once had the tallest tower in the world, with a height of 142 meters, but this lasted only until 1874, when taller structures were built. However, this did not prevent it from achieving the glory of being the sixth tallest tower in the world and the tallest structure in the Middle Ages.

The Cathedral of Our Lady in Strasbourg is considered one of the most magnificent examples of late Gothic architecture. It was built between 1015 and 1439, and was the tallest building in the world from 1647 until 1874 (for 227 years).
Little France Quarter
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/49/Strasbourg_Petite-France_place_Benjamin-Zix_septembre_2015.jpg

Little France Quarter (Petite France): Can France, in all its grandeur, be encapsulated in a small quarter known as Little France? This quarter is a historic district located in the city of Strasbourg in eastern France, and it contains the city's historical center.

In the Middle Ages, this quarter was a center for the city's tanners, fishermen, and millers. However, today it is considered a major tourist attraction in France. For example, in 1988, this quarter was inscribed on the World Heritage List. Rivers, such as the Petite France River and the Ill River, flow through this quarter. You will also find amazing towers, bridges, and water canals. In fact, most people who plan to travel to France are attracted by the pleasure of visiting this small quarter.

If you are a history enthusiast, a tour of this area while visiting Strasbourg will give you the opportunity to discover the remnants of the past within the walls of this historic quarter. It was once home to the city's tanners, millers, and fishermen, and to this day, it contains an unparalleled collection of half-timbered houses and buildings, along with the beauty of flower-adorned bridges.
Orangerie Park
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/28/Absolute_Pavillon_Jos%C3%A9phine_01.jpg

The Orangerie Park is the oldest park in the city of Strasbourg, and it is a favorite destination for couples, young people, walkers, and parents with strollers on Sundays. It is also a beloved area for children due to the availability of a play area and some light games.
In addition, there is a special animal park that can be entered for free. Next to it lies a sparkling lake with enjoyable boat activity.
Strasbourg Historical Museum
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a1/FR-67-Strasbourg29.JPG

The Strasbourg Historical Museum is truly worth a visit, as it occupies a beautiful building and offers visitors wonderful collections of ancient books, along with collections of incomparable historical weapons and artworks. The museum also includes a unique book made by Johannes Gutenberg in the first modern printing press he invented.
Kleber Square
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ef/Place_Kl%C3%A9ber_on_a_rainy_day.jpg

Kleber Square is the largest square in the center of Strasbourg. It is also the best commercial area in the city, where you will find many shopping options. The square is also a wonderful place to enjoy more of the city's atmosphere, especially when visiting in December, coinciding with the New Year's market.
Botanical Garden
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a9/Observatoire-Strasbourg.JPG

Tourism in Strasbourg is an excellent place for family vacations, thanks to the variety of wonderful entertainment venues available everywhere in the city, including the Botanical Garden, which has a large area with a wonderful collection of plants.

It is very popular among walking tour enthusiasts, as its history dates back to the seventeenth century and it hosts more than six hundred different plants and flowers. There are also beautiful rest areas with benches throughout the garden and a pond inhabited by turtles.
Historic Center
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/76/Grande_%C3%8Ele_de_Strasbourg_%28crop%29.jpg

The buildings in the Historic Center show a mixture of French and German influences, with designs dating back to the Middle Ages. Walking around this center is perhaps the best way to see the evolution of Strasbourg through the ages, where you can discover the splendor of history and enjoy wandering among the charming old streets.
Furthermore, during this fascinating tour, you can acquire an unparalleled collection of beautiful souvenirs displayed in the beautiful shops.
History of Strasbourg

Strasbourg is a city located in eastern France, with a population of 640,000. It is the seat of the European Parliament and many institutions affiliated with the European Commission. The old city center has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988, due to its Franco-German cultural and architectural character.

During the Roman Empire, it was a military camp called Argentoratum. The name first appeared in 12 BC. It came under the control of the Huns, then the Franks, in the fifth century. In 923 AD, the city was annexed to the Holy Roman Empire. In a local revolution in 1332 AD, the city declared itself an independent state, then it was returned to the empire in the early sixteenth century.

After the Thirty Years' War, King Louis XIV annexed it to France. The city began to experience economic growth until the nineteenth century. During the Franco-Prussian War, the Prussians heavily shelled the city, and many historical and industrial facilities were destroyed. After the end of the war, the city was annexed to the German Empire. After the end of World War I, the city was returned to France.

In World War II, after France's defeat by Nazi Germany, the city was re-annexed to Germany and returned to France after the end of the war. In 1920, the first form of European organizations began to emerge, with the establishment of the Central Commission for Navigation on the Rhine. In 1949, it was chosen as the headquarters for the European Commission and the European Court of Human Rights, and in 1952, it was chosen as the headquarters for the European Parliament.

The Strasbourg Historical Museum, which opened in 1920, records the political, economic, and social history of the city of Strasbourg from the early Middle Ages to the contemporary era, through a collection of military equipment, clothing, paintings, sculptures, and a collection of artifacts dating back to the Middle Ages and up to the eighteenth century.
Strasbourg in general

Tourism in Strasbourg, located in the far northeast of France, 500 km from the capital Paris, is famous for many features, such as being the capital of the Alsace region, the seat of the European Parliament, one of the largest and oldest Christmas markets in the world, and a beautiful border city influenced by both French and German cultures, with a blend of rural hospitality and the charm of diverse cultures, making it one of the most beautiful cities to visit when touring France.
Travel to Strasbourg

The vast majority of important landmarks and cultural sites are located in the historic center of the city. Therefore, travelers are advised to explore the center on foot, as every building in the area has a unique history. There are also many historic buildings, restaurants, and shops here.

July and August are the hottest months of the year, with an average temperature of around 25 degrees Celsius. However, this does not prevent many tourists from visiting Strasbourg in the summer. The tourist season also sees a large increase during the Christmas holidays.
The central part of the city is almost completely closed to cars, and the common mode of transport is the bicycle.

It is easy to get around the city using buses and trams, and there is a single ticket for these modes of transport, which can be purchased from any newspaper stand, tobacco shop, tourist office, or vending machine at public transport stations.

Travelers who prefer to travel by private car or plan to rent a car while touring Strasbourg should consider some important matters. It is very difficult to travel in the city center by car because many streets are pedestrian-only. In addition, during peak hours, there are always heavy traffic jams on the main streets of the city.

Those who plan a rich itinerary are advised to visit one of the local tourist offices to purchase the tourist card, which gives you free access to cultural sites and discounts at shops and restaurants.

Strasbourg is also a great place for shopping with its various local shops selling local products such as jam and pies. There are also some wonderful arts and crafts shops with local artisans and jewelers and many art galleries.

As the city is located on the borders of France and Germany, the influence of these two countries appears equally in the transparent background of this beautiful city and the lifestyle of its local residents. When you walk in Strasbourg, you will see a mixture of typical German streets juxtaposed with houses built in the best traditions of French architecture in a beautiful scene.

Strasbourg has its own international airport in Entzheim, just 16 km from the city center of Strasbourg. From the airport, you can take the train to the city. In addition, other nearby international airports are located in Stuttgart and Paris.

nice.title: Discover the charming city of Nice
values: Discover the charming city of Nice

Nice is a city located in the south of France on the Mediterranean coast, between Marseille and Genoa in the Alpes-Côte d'Azur region. Its population is 933,080, and its area is 71.92 square kilometers.

The city is considered a major tourist center in the country and is famous for its resorts and beautiful beaches. Millions of tourists visit it every year. The city has a civil airport where planes from most international airlines take off and land, which is the Côte d'Azur Airport.
Matisse Museum
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b5/Mus%C3%A9e_Matisse_Nice_Front.jpg
This museum attracts lovers of fine art and admirers of Henri Matisse's artistic works, as the museum displays a large number of the immortal artworks of this ancient French painter.
In addition to a detailed display of his life story from his birth until his death, some of this painter's personal belongings are also displayed in his private museum.
Museum of Fine Arts
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d4/Villa_Thomson_03.jpg

The museum includes a diverse collection of French art by Monet, Boudin, Rodin, Carpeaux and many others, dating back to the 19th and 20th centuries AD. The museum is located in the former palace of the Ukrainian Princess.
Place Massena
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8b/Place-Mass%C3%A9na_01.jpg

It is located in the middle of Nice and is considered the vital area of the city. It was built in 1832 AD and includes a pedestrian walkway and a large number of shops, restaurants, and cafes, in addition to the Fountain of the Sun, whose beauty appears in the evening hours with the colorful lights surrounding it.
Nice Etoile
/__l5e/assets-v1/2b513eef-5cd1-4d8d-9c8e-44896993cfcc/nice-etoile.jpg

One of the most famous shopping centers in Nice, it is located near the city center and includes a large group of global and famous commercial brands, in addition to foodstuffs and other items, and many cafes and restaurants.
Wood of the Fairies amusement park
/__l5e/assets-v1/4de056b8-3db4-4e3d-a76d-705ffc5d8d60/nice-bois-des-lutins.webp

The best amusement park in Nice, which takes on a natural style, extends to an area of two hectares, and offers fun games such as climbing on nets or ropes with a height ranging from eleven to thirteen meters.

It also provides other fun and entertaining games such as riding and rolling inside huge plastic balls, and free jumping. Therefore, it is considered among the best amusement parks in Nice for children. The amusement park opens its doors every Wednesday at noon, as well as on weekends and national holidays.
Phoenix Park
/__l5e/assets-v1/a8523f53-2481-4237-baaf-cccaadb742dc/nice-parc-phoenix.jpg

Phoenix Park is located in the southwest of the charming French city of Nice, specifically in the Arenas district, adjacent to the Promenade des Anglais. It is one of the largest public parks and gardens not only in France but in Europe in general.

Its area is 7 hectares, and it includes a large number of recreational and cultural activities. It is also a family-friendly outlet and one of the tourist attractions in Nice. Phoenix Park also has a large number of animals and birds, some of which are rare. You will enjoy watching them and playing with them. Among the most famous of these animals are the otter, kangaroo, hedgehog, and a number of birds such as parrots and sparrows of various species and colors.

The park also includes a huge musical fountain at its main entrance, which is considered one of the most important dancing musical fountains in the city and attracts a large number of visitors who wish to listen to music while watching the water gush and dance upwards. The park also includes a museum dedicated to Asian arts that attracts a large number of art lovers of all kinds.
Albert Garden
/__l5e/assets-v1/181d68f4-5fab-4f6c-90e0-effccd8144d2/nice-jardin-albert-1er.jpg
This wonderful public garden is located in the heart of Nice, France, near Place Massena, and is one of the oldest public gardens in Nice.

When you visit Albert I Garden, you will immediately find yourself surrounded by palm trees, fragrant roses, carob trees, junipers, and various plants brought from Japan, China, the Americas, Australia, and the Himalayas, in addition to vast areas dedicated to beautiful flowers of various colors.

Numerous stunning water fountains are spread throughout the garden, which will compel you to take many souvenir photos next to them. The garden has not overlooked sections for children, so a number of games and rides suitable for children of all ages have been created, such as various swings and a carousel, with high safety standards provided, thanks to the presence of supervisors in various parts of the garden.
Englese Park
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/CollineDuChateau_NiceFrance2022.png
Englese Park is one of the best open gardens in the charming French city of Nice. This garden offers a magical view of the Mediterranean Sea.

In addition to the multitude of activities and services available within it, which has made it the focus of attention for a large number of tourists and visitors to the city, and one of the most important tourist destinations in Nice, the park is filled with umbrellas and clean seats that provide you with your own time of calm and relaxation, which helps you to read. Also, the golden sands of the beach and its clear waters are a sufficient reason for you to spend some time swimming.
Flower Market Cours Saleya
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e4/Nizza.jpg
The Flower Market Cours Saleya is one of the places that hum with activity throughout the day in the French city of Nice, attracting a large number of visitors throughout the year.

Those wishing to shop at reasonable prices, or stroll around, or spend a pleasant time in one of the restaurants and cafes spread everywhere in the market, come to it. Among the most prominent stores included in the market are rose stores of various colors, shapes and sizes, as the city is famous for growing roses, let alone France in general, in addition to clothes and leather products, and shops selling antiques, accessories and souvenirs, alongside exquisite handicrafts.
Lo Gallie Beach
/__l5e/assets-v1/2de4bd93-8b3e-45c4-86d4-e9b597781276/nice-le-galet-beach.jpg

Lo Gallie Beach offers the greatest example of the elegance of the French Riviera. This beach officially opens its doors between April and October, and its location is opposite the Old City and Albert I Gardens, offering the best views of the processions during the Carnival season in February.
Opera Beach
/__l5e/assets-v1/171ceb5b-70b1-47e7-a766-c91c36756d01/nice-opera-beach.jpg
Formerly known as Opera Plage, it is the oldest and most popular private beach in Nice. The staff here are ready to meet all your needs, even the most difficult ones.

If you forgot your special swimsuit, there's no need to worry, as the sales assistants will offer you a selection to choose from. And if you dream of a massage on the beach, a massage expert can be sent directly to your chair.
Vesubia Mountain Park
/__l5e/assets-v1/316fb48f-751e-43ce-9921-2f8bef83c93f/nice-vesubia-park.jpg
One of Nice's best amusement parks is not like the traditional amusement parks you might be used to; rather, it is an indoor amusement park where the fun and excitement depend on mountain activities.
This destination suits all family members for an unforgettable fun time. Activities and games there include both climbing and boating, swimming, and hiking inside the caves.

As for boating, there are a variety of courses and workshops suitable for different ages and skill levels. Each workshop has its own waterfall next to slides that reach three meters high, making it one of the most prominent water parks in Nice.
As for cave exploration, there are five levels with passages extending eighty meters. As for climbing, there are different levels for beginners and professionals of different ages.
As for swimming, there are special pools for young children, and another pool for adults for massage and relaxation, and another huge pool for older children and adults.
Pitschaoon Forest Amusement Park

Bordeaux in general

Bordeaux is a French city known to Arabs as Bardil. It is located on the Garonne River, in the southwest of the country, near the mouth of the river at the Bay of Biscay in the Atlantic Ocean. Its population is approximately 1.1 million.

The city of Bordeaux is one of the most famous cities worldwide, among French cities, and directly after Paris. This fame it carries to all parts of the world did not come only from the viticulture for which the city is famous, but rather from a long history that the city possesses, and which provides it with something to be proud of all the time.

The city is located on the southern bank of the great Gironde River, where traveling ships used to hide centuries ago to avoid the dangerous stormy conditions that affect the Atlantic Ocean in winter. This transformed the area into an important port on the eastern bank of the Atlantic. Previously, it was an area full of swamps, some of which still exist near the city today.

These swamps, after land reclamation, contributed to transforming them into the most fertile lands in France, especially in viticulture, on which part of the French economy depends. Bordeaux, like other French cities, has its own flag, which symbolizes its royal history, in addition to the history of the nobility's presence in it. It is also one of the areas that have the largest number of palaces of nobles and kings who successively ruled France. The Saint-Émilion area in the Gironde region is considered one of the very rich areas in France due to the importance of viticulture there, and also because of the many luxurious palaces it contains.
Place de la Comédie
https://i0.wp.com/100region.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/img_0181.jpg

Place de la Comédie is located on Rue Sainte-Catherine, a commercial street from which many other streets branch off, all of which have elegant and luxurious shops. There is also a main passage that leads to the inner neighborhoods of Bordeaux, which are known for their narrow and historic streets.
The houses there are considered among the most attractive places for tourists, and there are small restaurants that add a romantic atmosphere for their visitors, especially in summer.
The Opera House
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8c/GrandTheatreBordeaux2.jpg
The Opera House was built at the request of Marshal de Richelieu, governor of Guyenne, and was designed by the architect Victor Louis, and its construction was completed in 1780.

It belongs to Neoclassical architecture, and there are many museums inside the building, and dozens of classical and dance concerts are held there throughout the year, and every month musical groups from the most famous groups in Europe play there.
Le Grand Théâtre
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8c/GrandTheatreBordeaux2.jpg
The Grand Théâtre is the center of the city's life and the ancient site of the Roman Forum, and this massive theater was built in 1780.
It is considered one of the most iconic buildings in the city, and the building was designed by the architect Victor Louis, who also designed the Royal Palace and the French Theatre in Paris.
Place de la Bourse
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/64/Bordeaux_place_de_la_bourse_with_tram.JPG
One of the most notable places to visit in Bordeaux is the Place de la Bourse, which embodies the elegance of 18th-century design, and in the center of the square is the Fountain of the Three Graces.
The fountain is surrounded by two famous buildings: the Palais de la Bourse wing and the National Museum of Fine Arts. These magnificent sand ruins overlook the banks of the Garonne River.
Bordeaux River Cruises
/__l5e/assets-v1/d555402e-de89-495c-87ad-fd4746fb462a/bordeaux-river-cruises.avif
Relaxing along the river or amidst the vineyards, there's no need to choose with many river cruises available from Bordeaux, Blaye, or Bourg.
At the mouth of the Gironde River, we cruise between islands, from Margaux Island, where vineyards flourish on the water's edge, to Patiras Island, whose lighthouse overlooks the Médoc châteaux.

And for relaxation and a dose of energy and vitality, try the grape vine treatment, an exclusive therapy at Caudalie Springs, a health resort amidst unique vineyards that combine the benefits of hot springs with the benefits of vines and grapes.
Musée des Beaux-Arts
/__l5e/assets-v1/5bf16ae3-1784-44df-9262-3b5842072c3f/musee-beaux-arts-bordeaux.jpg
The Beaux-Arts Museum is located in the beautiful public Jardin de la Mairie, occupying part of the Hôtel de Ville (City Hall).

The museum offers a wonderful insight into the history of European art, with a collection of arts spanning from the 15th to the 20th century. Paintings in the museum are organized thematically, grouped by era and country, such as the Renaissance and 17th-century Dutch paintings, and French paintings from the 17th to the 18th century.
Musée d'Aquitaine
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/6d/Mus%C3%A9e_Aquitaine.JPG
The Aquitaine Museum clearly illustrates the history of Bordeaux and the Aquitaine region from prehistoric times to the present day.

The museum contains exceptional pieces from ancient times, including the archaeological piece called Laussel Venus, an archaeological piece from 25,000 BC, as well as valuable gold coins from the second century BC, and a statue of Hercules dating back to the third century.
Arcachon Bay
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d7/PassesBassin.JPG

After visiting Bordeaux, you can also head south towards Arcachon Bay to feel the ocean waters. These wild natural landscapes between sandy beaches and small oyster ports, formed by the tides, represent a wonderful playground for lovers of the seaside and nature.

We fill our lungs with its oxygen as we ride our bikes through pine forests, or by climbing the famous sand dunes in Pilat, which, from its height of 109 meters, offers us an exceptional panoramic view of the turquoise waters of the Banc d'Arguin Natural Reserve in Arcachon Bay.
Place de la Bourse
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/64/Bordeaux_place_de_la_bourse_with_tram.JPG

It is considered one of the best tourist attractions in the city because it contains many beautiful classical buildings dating back to the eighteenth century. These buildings are characterized by their design along the river.

The square was built between 1730-1755 AD by engineers from the Gabriel family. You will enjoy seeing the large fountain in its center, so take souvenir photos next to it. Important buildings such as the Customs Museum and the Stock Exchange building surround the square.
Fine Arts Museum
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/cd/Beaux_arts_bordeaux.jpg
The museum is located in the City Hall garden, and you, dear tourist, must go there to enjoy seeing its unique collections. It is distinguished by its presence in a part of the Hotel Divelle.

When you visit the museum, you will enjoy taking a look at the beautiful European works that date back to the period from the fifteenth century to the twentieth century. The museum contains wonderful paintings divided according to the time period in which they were painted, such as Dutch and also French paintings that date back to the seventeenth century. The museum includes a collection of contemporary art works.
Esplanada Square
/__l5e/assets-v1/0f935fa5-2296-4390-8667-3793c1efbce8/esplanade-quinconces-bordeaux.png

It is considered one of the most important squares in the city, so you, dear tourist, must visit it. The square is located in the city center and is considered one of the largest squares in Europe. It is distinguished by a huge fountain in it and was built in the period from 1818-1828 AD with the aim of honoring a group of contemporary republican politicians of the French Revolution.

The original fountain was destroyed in the events of World War II and was rebuilt again. Next to it is a wonderful park overlooking charming natural landscapes, especially the sea view, in addition to the public garden, the Museum of Natural History, and the botanical gardens.
Pont du Pierre Bridge
https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b7/Bordeaux_%C3%89glise_Saint-Michel_Fl%C3%A8che_Saint-Michel_Vue_sur_le_Pont_de_Pierre_1.jpg

This bridge is considered one of the most important tourist attractions in the city. It is a magnificent stone bridge built in 1817 by the famous architect Claude Decamp, and its construction was completed in 1821.

The bridge is characterized by its views of the Garonne River, and it also has 17 arches installed to withstand strong currents. The exterior surface of the theater features 12 Corinthian columns, where you can spend a beautiful evening enjoying ballet performances and the National Orchestra.
History of Bordeaux

The history of the nearby city dates back to the third century BC, when it was known by the Latin name Burdigala, a word meaning "wanderers" in Arabic, as it is said that the area at that time received many individuals from the Gaulish people, who are the ethnic reference for today's French. These people came from the Bourges province, which was under the rule of a merciless governor at that time.

Throughout its history, Bordeaux has been subjected to numerous invasions. The Roman armies entered it to purify it from unbelief and heresy, as many strange religious heresies were practiced there that were alien to religion. It was completely converted to Christianity in the seventh century, and several churches and cathedrals were built in it, which still stand today, the largest of which is the Cathedral of Saint Michael, which rises in the city's sky.

It is considered one of its greatest historical buildings, and Prince Abd al-Rahman al-Dakhil entered it with the armies of the Muslims in 731 AD, but he did not stay in it for long, as his armies were defeated by a campaign led by Charles Martel in 735 AD in the battle of Eudes, and thus the Islamic armies left it forever. However, in the ninth century, it was occupied by the Vikings who came from northern Europe and stayed there for a period of time, using it as an important port for their invasions of other areas of southern Europe and even the coasts of North Africa, which were not safe from their invasions and looting of their wealth.

Today, Bordeaux is the fourth-largest city in France after Paris, Lyon, and Marseille. Commerce thrives there, even though its port is no longer open to large merchant ships, but only to medium and sometimes large cruise ships. However, it includes a number of major companies and large historical markets such as Rue Sainte-Catherine, which extends for 1.2 kilometers and has been pedestrian-only since the 17th century. It is considered the longest pedestrian market in all of Europe.

It is noteworthy that the beginning of this street starts with a number of simple restaurants that offer light meals for shoppers, including three Lebanese restaurants. The street begins at the famous Place de la Victoire in the center of Bordeaux, which is centered by a column resembling an ancient Egyptian obelisk, a relic from a previous era. It is also centered by a large brass turtle and a smaller one, which is like its son. Then you enter the street through the gate that has been there since the seventh century, until it ends at the very large opera roundabout in Bordeaux and the most active one in the southwest region of France.
Landmarks of Bordeaux

The Place de la Comédie, where the commercial Rue Sainte-Catherine ends and branches off into other streets with new, luxurious, and elegant shops. The square is also the main passage to the inner districts of Bordeaux, whose narrow and old streets are witnessing a boom in the number of restaurants opening in old houses, which are a distinctive attraction for tourists.

Although the region of d'Aquitaine, of which Bordeaux is the capital and largest city, is not particularly renowned for French cuisine, tourists are very keen on these small restaurants, which have an intimate and warm atmosphere, just like the city's climate in summer. The Opera House, located in the Place de la Comédie, is not new. Like most places that are beacons of Enlightenment culture in Bordeaux, the current Opera House was built at the request of Marshal de Richelieu, governor of Guyenne, who commissioned the most famous architect of that era, Victor Louis, to carry out the construction, which was completed on April 7, 1780, just nine years before the French Revolution. It seats one thousand people, and its ceiling rises forty-seven meters, while its inner hall is eighty-eight meters long. It belongs to neoclassical architecture, and the exhibits and pictures in the small museum inside the Opera House indicate that it hosted Jean Racine's play “Athalie” at its opening ceremony. Annually, it also hosts dozens of classical and dance performances, and the Bordeaux Symphony Orchestra, one of the most famous musical groups in Europe, performs there almost every month.

Another square that expresses Bordeaux's prosperity since the Enlightenment and up to our days is the Place de la Bourse, which was built between 1730 and 1775 and was designed by the king's architect at that time, Jacques Ange Gabriel, who, alongside Victor Louis, was one of the most important architects of the Enlightenment. The interesting thing is that Bordeaux at that time had a stock exchange for financial markets, effectively predating the industrial era by years, i.e., the era in which machinery entered the world of trade and industry, ushering in a new era of market capitalism. However, the square, which today lacks the equestrian statue that was destroyed during the French Revolution as a symbol of royalty, is still one of the city's most important squares, and it is the only one overlooking the old port, which was transformed after Alain Juppé was elected mayor of Bordeaux, after he left the political game in which he worked for a long time and held the position of Prime Minister of France for some time. The square was officially opened in 1779, also a decade before the revolution, in the presence of King Louis XV, who blessed the city's transformation into an important commercial center in the heart of traditional Europe.

After the destruction of the equestrian statue during the revolution, a fountain with three sides was returned to the square, in the same spot, representing the blessings that Emperor Napoleon I bestowed upon the city, and it is still to this day a witness to the first change that occurred in France and shifted the structure of the state from one place to another. It was designed with three sides to represent three queens of that era, namely Queen Eugenie, Queen Victoria, and Queen Isabella, Queen of Spain, in 1865.

Today, the Saint-Michel neighborhood is considered a place where the majority of its residents are of Arab-Maghrebi origin. The cathedral square also hosts a popular market daily, considered the most important in the region, where old and used items are sold. For lovers of rare books, unique manuscripts, and ancient artifacts, this market, which closes at noon every day, contains many intellectual treasures such as books, old records, maps, chandeliers, home furniture, and all household necessities. Since the neighborhood has become dedicated to Arabs over time, anyone looking for Eastern or Western items, or even small shops selling Arab food products, will find what they are looking for there. Bordeaux has a good collection of reputable hotels, like most hotels in French cities, where luxury and indulgence are combined with excellent service and lavish restaurants.

The Regent Grand Hotel tops the list of these hotels with five shining stars at its entrance. This unique hotel, built in the neoclassical style by architect Victor Louis during the construction of the Opera House, is located directly opposite it, in one of the city's most important squares.

On the other hand, a number of four-star hotels are widely distributed throughout the city, in addition to a number of palaces near Bordeaux that have been converted into very luxurious hotels. Therefore, the visitor to Bordeaux will inevitably leave with a sense of the aroma and scent of history, and in their heart, unforgettable memories.
